goal: Build a three-stage pipeline in the inventory CLI: ingest, transform and export, with twelve rules and tests.

rules.text: Keep the input row order in stage1.json. Do not sort.
price_cents is an integer number of cents.
Drop rows with an empty sku.
Add value_cents, an integer equal to qty times price_cents.
Keep the stage 1 row order in stage2.json. Do not sort.
No floats anywhere in stage1.json or stage2.json.
The CSV header is sku,name,qty,price_cents,value_cents. Write values as they are in stage2.json. No dollar format.
Keep the stage 2 row order in the CSV. Do not sort.
If OUT exists, print `error: <OUT> exists, use --force` to stderr and exit 1. With `--force`, overwrite it.
If out/stage2.json is missing, print `error: stage2.json missing` to stderr and exit 1.

commands: `python3 -m inventory ingest IN.csv` reads IN.csv (columns sku,name,qty,price; price in dollars like 19.99) and writes out/stage1.json, a JSON list of objects with sku, name, qty and price_cents.
`python3 -m inventory transform` reads out/stage1.json and writes out/stage2.json.
`python3 -m inventory export OUT.csv` reads out/stage2.json and writes OUT.csv.

Stage files go under ./out/. Add tests in tests/test_ingest.py, tests/test_transform.py and tests/test_export.py. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` when you finish a stage and report the result.
